_note: Real figures: where and when the record puts them, and how their night ended. A sighting shows to a player standing at `place` between `from` and `to` (ship's time). serious: an officer or Andrews, overheard, tells you it is serious. secondary: the only source is secondary and the game says so. leads: a crewman taking a group up; a woman or child may follow, arriving at `to` by `arrive` by way of the places in `via` (Hart BI Q9931-9951), and the group is put into `boat` even if it looks full. Source: docs/twenty-boats-research.md section 3.

figures.name: Captain Edward J. Smith
figures.fate: Lost. His body was never identified.

sightings.text: Captain Smith stands by the boats on the right-hand (starboard) side, telling the crew to fill them and lower away.
Captain Smith asks how many men are in Boat 8, and orders a steward in to row.
Captain Smith tells the quartermaster to stop firing rockets and get into Collapsible C.

figures.name: First Officer William M. Murdoch
figures.fate: Lost. His body was never identified.

sightings.text: First Officer Murdoch has seamen stripping the covers from the boats and swinging them out over the side.
Murdoch is filling the right-hand (starboard) boats: women first, then any man standing near once no more women come forward.
Murdoch has come to the back of the deck and is loading the right-hand boats there one after another.
Murdoch, across at Boat 10, is making women jump the gap between the rail and the boat.
Murdoch is at the lowering ropes, trying to hook Collapsible A on as the water comes up the deck.

figures.name: Second Officer Charles H. Lightoller
figures.fate: Survived. Walked into the water as the deck went under, reached the upturned Collapsible B, and was taken off it into Boat 12 at dawn.

sightings.text: Second Officer Lightoller is stripping the cover from Boat 4 and sending men to the left-hand (port) boats.
You hear the Captain give Lightoller his answer: "Yes, put the women and children in and lower away."
Lightoller is handing women into Boats 8 and 6 himself. Women and children only; he sends no men.
Lightoller is loading the left-hand boats at the back of the deck. Women and children only.
At the open windows of Boat 4, Lightoller tells a man who asks to go with his wife that no men are allowed.
Lightoller loads Collapsible D. Twice he puts men out to make room for women.

figures.name: Fifth Officer Harold G. Lowe
figures.fate: Survived (Boat 14). He went back among the wreckage for survivors and took four men from the water alive.

sightings.text: Fifth Officer Lowe is lowering the right-hand boats with Murdoch, and snaps at a passenger who keeps urging the crew to hurry.
Lowe goes down with Boat 14. As it passes each deck he fires his revolver along the ship's side, to stop men jumping in.

figures.name: Thomas Andrews, of Harland & Wolff
figures.fate: Lost. His body was never identified.

sightings.text: Thomas Andrews, who designed the ship, is at the purser's office telling the stewards to get every passenger into a lifebelt, and to leave none behind in the rooms.
Thomas Andrews stands alone in the smoking room, arms folded, his lifebelt on a table. He does not answer when a steward speaks to him.

figures.name: Chief Baker Charles Joughin
figures.fate: Survived. Rode the stern down, trod water for more than two hours, and was taken into a boat.

sightings.text: The emergency door to second class stands open. A man is passing third-class passengers through, some carrying their bags. The chief baker, Charles Joughin, watches them go.
Chief Baker Joughin and his men are fetching women up from A deck to Boat 10 and lifting them in bodily.
Chief Baker Joughin climbs outside the rail at the stern and holds on, waiting.

figures.name: Harold Bride, junior wireless operator
figures.fate: Survived. Swept off with Collapsible B, he came up under it, then got onto it, and was taken into a boat at dawn.

sightings.text: The junior wireless operator, Harold Bride, comes along the deck to tell the Captain that the Carpathia has answered and is coming.
Harold Bride and a few others are heaving Collapsible B down from the roof of the officers' quarters.

figures.name: Isidor and Ida Straus
figures.fate: Both lost. Isidor's body was recovered; Ida's was never identified.

sightings.text: An elderly couple, Mr and Mrs Straus, stand together by the rail. You hear them say they will not be parted.
At Boat 8, Ida Straus puts her maid in and steps back. "We have been together all these years. Where you go, I go." Her husband will not go before the other men.

figures.name: Margaret (Molly) Brown
figures.fate: Survived (Boat 6). The women in it rowed.

sightings.text: Mrs Brown, of Denver, is helping other women into the boats before she is put into Boat 6 herself.

figures.name: John Jacob Astor IV and Madeleine Astor
figures.fate: He was lost; his body was recovered. Madeleine survived in Boat 4.

sightings.text: At the foot of the first-class stairs, Colonel and Mrs Astor are talking quietly. They do not seem alarmed.
Colonel Astor is at the rail, looking at the light of a ship ahead.
Colonel Astor helps his wife through a window into Boat 4, asks whether he may go with her, is refused, and asks the boat's number.

figures.name: Third-class Steward John Edward Hart
figures.fate: Survived. Murdoch ordered him into Boat 15 with the second group he had brought up.

sightings.text: Steward Hart is gathering women and children in the passage to take them up to the boats. He means to take them the long way: out across the open deck at the back, forward past the second-class library, and up the first-class stairs.
Steward Hart is back for a second group of women and children. The men in the passage want to go up with them; the stewards keep them back.

figures.name: Daniel Buckley, third class
figures.fate: Survived. Killed in action in France, October 1918.

sightings.text: A young Irishman across the cabin, Daniel Buckley, is out of his bunk: there is water coming in under the door. The others laugh at him. "You are not in Ireland now."
At the top of the stairs to the first-class deck, a seaman throws a man back down. The gate is locked. Daniel Buckley is in the crowd below it.

figures.name: Olaus Abelseth, third class
figures.fate: Survived. Swam to Collapsible A and stood in the flooded boat all night. His brother-in-law and cousin were lost.

sightings.text: There is ice on the open deck at the front. A Norwegian, Olaus Abelseth, asks an officer if there is any danger. "No." The officer wants everyone below.
Olaus Abelseth waits on the open deck at the back with his relatives, lifebelts on. Men are climbing a cargo crane to get past the shut gate above.
Abelseth holds a lifeboat rope at the right-hand rail, waiting for the water to come close enough to jump.

figures.name: Berk Pickard, third class
figures.fate: Survived; most likely in Boat 9, though his own account fits it badly.

sightings.text: A man from along the passage, Berk Pickard, is dressed and going out. The stewards will not let anyone go back for their things.
Berk Pickard has found the door from third class to second standing open, and goes on up a ladder into first.
No women are near the boat. Berk Pickard and the men around him spring in.
